paper_title: Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models
caption: The effect of and by language family. Error bars indicate the standard deviation.
model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the effect of various language families on different models, comparing the "mBERT-targ", "XLM-targ", "mBERT-permute", and "XLM-permute" models across nine language families. The horizontal axis lists the language families, including IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic, while the vertical axis represents the "effect" with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 40. Each language family is associated with a group of four bars, colored light blue, dark blue, light green, and dark green, representing the four models, with "mBERT-targ" and "XLM-targ" generally having higher values than "mBERT-permute" and "XLM-permute". The "Isolate" family has the tallest "mBERT-targ" bar at approximately 33, while "IE-Indic" has the tallest "mBERT-permute" bar at around 16; in contrast, "Isolate" has one of the shortest "mBERT-permute" and "XLM-permute" bars, both at approximately 2. Error bars indicating standard deviation are present for each bar, extending upwards from the top of each bar. The bars are grouped by language family, with the four models represented by different colors, and are not sorted in a specific order. Some bars have relatively high values, such as "Uralic" for "mBERT-targ" at around 28 and "IE-Baltic" for "XLM-targ" at approximately 15.
